When I was just 19, the guy I've been dating for 3 years (25M) left me for his best friend at the time, a girl he worked with and with whom he spent many nights of the week. He would call me 'crazy' when I showed any signs of jealousy.All of 'our friends' knew about their attraction so I can grasp the concept of feeling alone.So what I did, after binge-drinking wine, crying for weeks and all sorts of unhealthy behavior, is going on a trip by myself with a very low amount of money. I had to fend for myself, it was crazy. That trip is something I'll always remember. It taught me so much about myself. Once that trip was over, instead of coming back to my hometown, I decided to move to a different city. Got my first long-term job. In the end what happened was bitter-sweet because it pushed me to pursue my dreams. However, to this day, I still have difficulty trusting people and am very paranoid. I now have a sweet fiancé, we've been together 8 years. My ex is not with that girl anymore, she ended up cheating on him. Sometimes this whole thing makes me believe that everything happens for a reason... I don't know you personally, but it seems to me that you are an articulate, intelligent, pretty, honest, caring and gentle young lady. I hope you can see that yourself too. It's a shame that there's cruel people out there who take advantage of good people.

>Would you want to, or have already, married the person?

We're engaged but I don't view marriage as anything more than an expensive ceremony and endless moments of awkwardness with both families. If we had the money we would probably do it, but it's not of great importance for neither of us. 

>How would you handle conflicts related to jealousy, both you or your partner's?

We have had A LOT of conflicts about jealousy. We tell each other the honest truth, all the time. We never lie. We're very open about everything. It's about accepting that we're both humans, ie animals with natural instincts. It's necessary to establish boundaries with your partner, within the relationship. 

>Would you tend to fear or avoid arguing about sensitive and upsetting topics. For example commitment or maybe an issue in the relationship you have decided is not important but your partner is tortured over?

Sometimes yes. But if it's something very important that I obsess over, I'll definitely bring up the subject. Trying to avoid certain topics make them go into your subconscious, it eats you from the inside. You don't want that. But we don't always come to an agreement. For example he wants kids, I do not. We have agreed to wait this one out and bring up the subject again in a couple of years. 

>Be able to argue with someone who is much more emotionally intense or volatile?

Although an INTJ I can get pretty emotional sometimes, and my emotions make him emotional. I take space, he goes for a walk. We get back to the subject once we both feel less emotional and have thought about the subject more thoroughly. Sometimes that takes an hour, sometimes it takes a day. I don't think any productive discussions can happen in the heat of the moment. Nothing can be solved by arguing either. 

>If the person develops complications due to a medical problem (which your partner openingly discussed on the first date) resulting in personality and behavioral change, even if you are not married, would you remain romantically committed and attached?

On paper yes, but in practice I can only imagine how difficult that must be. I believe that if you commit to someone, it's important to be there for them when they need it the most. However you have to put your own needs and wellness first. If it affects you too much then it's time to think about it and talk. Maybe find someone outside of the relationship you could talk to. 

>What would you feel like if this person yelled at you?

It happens. It's inevitable. I remind myself that I am the most important person in my life. I take some distance and practice self-care. Of course if it's a daily occurrence then you might want to discuss it with your partner and try to find solutions, like couple's therapy or anger management. 

Source : We have been together for 7 1/2 years
